name: SPHEREx
best_known_for: NASA's all-sky infrared spectral survey: launched in March 2025, first full map finished in December 2025
credit: SPHEREx: launched 2025-03-12 at 03:10 UTC (11:10 p.m. EDT on 11 March), Falcon 9 Block 5, Vandenberg SLC-4E, rideshare with the four PUNCH smallsats; first_flight uses the UTC date. Sources: NASA/JPL SPHEREx quick facts and spacecraft pages, NASA/JPL first-map news release, Wikipedia. Status ACTIVE: operational per the December 2025 first-map release; nothing later (a second map, any anomaly) was found. Source conflicts: mass 502 kg (1,107 lb), 2.6 m tall and 3.2 m wide and deep from NASA quick facts, and Wikipedia agrees on 2.6 x 3.2 m; the quick-facts launch time is written 7:10 p.m. PST but the date was PDT, so the UTC time above comes from Wikipedia and the EDT time. The band count is 102 (NASA, six filters x 17) against 96 on Wikipedia; 102 is used. Altitude is 700 km at 97 degrees on Wikipedia against 650 km and dawn-dusk Sun-synchronous in a NASA press-kit snippet only; not resolved, not shown. The prime mission is 27 months including a month each of commissioning and decommissioning (NASA quick facts) against 25 months on Wikipedia; science operations began 2025-05-01 (Wikipedia) and NASA says mapping began in May. Telescope 20 cm aperture, field of view 11.3 x 3.5 deg, six 2048 x 2048 H2RG arrays; three photon shields about 19 mm thick, stack 1.7 m tall and 3.2 m across; solar array 2.67 x 1.02 m, about 750 W; cost about US$488 million; four all-sky maps planned. Bus builder BAE Systems, Boulder (formerly Ball); payload Caltech / JPL; data at IPAC. Checked 2026-11-26.
